## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people divided by the combined number of employed and unemployed people. It does not include everyone who is not working: people outside the labor force are counted separately.

Whether someone is classified as unemployed depends on the survey’s reference period, the person’s availability for work, and the circumstances of their job search. A person who was not employed during the reference week, was available for work apart from a temporary illness, and was on temporary layoff expecting recall may count as unemployed without actively searching for a job.

Browsing job listings alone is different. It is considered passive-only search; active job-search efforts generally must take place during the four-week period ending with the reference week. So neither not working nor looking at listings, by itself, determines whether someone is counted as unemployed. The classification depends on meeting the active-search criteria or the temporary-layoff-and-recall condition, along with the applicable timing and availability criteria.
